live.name: Qakbot and Emotet
live.headline: Qakbot and Emotet: Two Information Stealers Aimed at Bank Logins and Business Networks
live.in_short: Windows Defender Research reported in November 2017 that Qakbot and Emotet steal online banking credentials and increasingly hit businesses. Machine encounters were trending upward.

sentences.t: Qakbot and Emotet are information stealers. Windows Defender Research reported renewed activity from both in the months before its report of 6 November 2017.
The report says the cybercriminals behind the two families have improved their code over the years.
The report's monthly chart of machine encounters shows an upward trend.
The malware is typically known to target individual online banking users.
The report says more and more enterprises, small and medium businesses, and other organizations have also been affected by indiscriminate infections.
The ultimate goal of both families is stealing online banking credentials that operators can then use. They can also steal other sensitive information with techniques such as keylogging.
The report says malicious emails carrying trojan droppers can install them. It also mentions malicious documents, such as those that use macro code, as a way of installing them.
Other malware can also spread them during the lateral movement stage of an attack. The report names DDEDownloader as a recent downloader that installs other malware.
The report cautions that some variants might not show all the described behaviors and might have unique routines. Its data also excludes variants blocked by automation and cloud rules.
Block malicious emails that carry trojan droppers, as the report advises.
The report suggests defenders watch for new service creations by tracking event ID 7045 in the system log. It also points to the Sysinternals Autoruns tool as a help.
